title: Restart the web application
content:
Use Nexus Control, never a shell, for routine restarts.

  1. Sign in as an Operator and open Nexus Control.
  2. Choose nexus-web and confirm the restart.
  3. Wait one minute and check Nexus Status.

If the status stays red, roll back with the steps in the rollback runbook.

content:
A rollback swaps the current and previous release folders and restarts the web application.

  2. Check /api/health/ready returns ready.

title: The Starting Point
content:
YTL Nexus began when Muammer (BSc IT Cloud Engineering, APU Malaysia) joined the YTL Communications IT Infrastructure team as an intern. Their Rocky Linux test host — now known as Nexus Core 01 — carried disconnected prototype pages and legacy test utilities from earlier experiments.

An initial host audit revealed severe security and reliability gaps in those drafts: custom PHP webmail running over plain HTTP with directory listings enabled, downloadable admin JSON and PHP backups, plaintext mailbox passwords stored in sessions, a passwordless root sudo helper, legacy ftpadmin and vsftpd configuration, an old WordPress install, an unused Podman container, MariaDB listening on all interfaces, an inactive firewall, and disabled NTP clock sync.

Rather than patching fragile legacy scripts, the team chose a clean-slate greenfield rebuild. Every old prototype was studied strictly for requirements, archived behind a verified preflight backup, and removed — keeping every team OS account and sssd configuration untouched, and reusing only yes-website-redesign/ as the read-only source for Yes Experience.

title: Architecture Decisions: The Cohesive Single Host
content:
YTL Nexus unifies 16 platform modules — across Explore, Operate, Services, and Govern, alongside self-service Account & Requests (/account) and hidden administrator governance — on a single Rocky Linux 9 server running Next.js 16.3.5, React 19, and Node.js 24 LTS:

  • Zero-Bypass Single-Hostname Routing: Apache 2.4 terminates TLS on one hostname and routes by path across Next.js (/*), headless WordPress (/studio), Roundcube Webmail (/webmail), and SFTPGo WebClient (/files), keeping every database, metric store, and local daemon bound strictly to loopback 127.0.0.1 or Unix sockets.
  • Five Isolated MariaDB Schemas & Eight Dual-Mode Adapters: Five separated MariaDB 10.5 databases (ytl_nexus, nexus_wordpress, nexus_roundcube, nexus_sftpgo, nexus_mail) prevent cross-service access, while all eight backing adapters (MariaDB, Better Auth, WordPress, Prometheus, Ollama, SFTPGo, nexus-ops, and Mail) implement matching live and deterministic demo implementations under NEXUS_MODE.
  • Unified Identity & Self-Service Lifecycle: Better Auth enforces four-tier RBAC (Viewer, Member, Operator, Administrator), public Stage 1 (Member) sign-up, three-stage promotion and service requests from /account, one-time SSO tickets for embedded Mail and Transfer portals, and append-only audit_events.
  • Adaptive Nexus Design & 3D WebGL Showcase: Built around Bricolage Grotesque, Figtree, and JetBrains Mono across three themes (Obsidian, Blueprint, and Daylight), paired with a lazy-loaded Three.js 3D particle rendering of the official Yes gradient logomark on /.
excerpt: YTL Nexus unifies 16 platform modules — across Explore, Operate, Services, and Govern, alongside self-service Account & Requests (/account)

title: Challenges Overcome
content:
Integrating eight backing adapters and eleven runtime daemons and timers on a single host required solving five real-world systems hurdles:

  • Privilege-Separated Host IPC (nexus-ops): Allowing operators to inspect bounded logs, run predefined health probes, and restart allowlisted systemd units without giving the web app sudo or shell access required a dedicated daemon listening on a Unix socket with HMAC-SHA256 signatures, bounded timestamps, single-use nonces, and polkit rules.
  • Local AI Without AVX/AVX2: Nexus Core 01 runs on 8 QEMU/KVM Westmere-class virtual CPUs without AVX/AVX2 vector extensions. Selecting quantized gemma3:1b-it-qat (~8.3 tok/s) alongside MariaDB BLOB vector storage and in-memory cosine search kept grounded runbook Q&A responsive without starving web requests.
  • Unified Mail & Transfer Provisioning: Linking SFTPGo quotas and SSH public keys plus Postfix/Dovecot virtual mailboxes to platform accounts required atomic API provisioning, one-time SSO ticket handoff, and strict credential separation so Next.js hashes never cross service databases.
  • Resilient Headless WordPress Pipeline: Bridging WordPress REST endpoints with Next.js caching via HMAC-signed /api/revalidate webhooks, paired with deterministic fixture fallbacks so /tour and /story never blank out even if CMS polling momentarily drops.
  • High-Density 3D WebGL Within Strict Budgets: Sampling up to 140,000 particles directly from the official Yes SVG, using camera.setViewOffset to prevent ultrawide perspective distortion, and blending dual-palette ambient dust shaders across dark and light modes — while keeping three completely absent from every other route bundle.

title: Security Lessons Learned
content:
Every security boundary in YTL Nexus was built from Task 1 and verified in a documented threat model rather than bolted on at the end:

  • Server-Authoritative RBAC & Hidden Governance: Every page, Route Handler, and Server Function enforces requireRole() and Zod schema validation independently on the server. Hidden administration routes return a byte-identical 404 to visitors and non-Administrators, while Administrators require enrolled TOTP 2FA and a 10-minute password-plus-TOTP Step-Up window.
  • Session Hardening & Brute-Force Lockout: Sessions expire after 60 minutes idle or 12 hours absolute with immediate database revocation. Five failed attempts within 15 minutes trigger a DB-backed lockout keyed on account and Apache's trusted X-Real-IP header, while every auth event and state change writes to append-only audit_events.
  • Network Perimeter, Sandboxing & Supply Chain: Only six ports (22, 80, 443, 587, 993, 2022) are open in firewalld; fail2ban protects sshd, postfix, and sftpgo; systemd units run hardened sandboxes (1.5–1.7 OK); per-request CSP nonces guard HTML responses; and gitleaks gates every commit.
  • Unidirectional Root Timers & Honest Posture Reporting: nexus-shield-scan, nexus-backup, and nexus-restore-test run via root systemd timers and write read-only reports or INSERT-only rows. All 11 Nexus Shield benchmarks explicitly surface accepted pilot risks — including disabled SELinux and SSH root/password flags — rather than hiding them or risking remote lockout with auto-remediation.
excerpt: Every security boundary in YTL Nexus was built from Task 1 and verified in a documented threat model rather than bolted on at the end:Server

title: Skills & Technical Growth
content:
Delivering a production-ready internal pilot end to end demanded deep systems engineering alongside frontend craft:

  • Linux Systems & Network Administration: Rocky Linux 9 baseline hardening, Apache 2.4 TLS termination and reverse path routing, systemd sandboxing and timers, polkit, Postfix/Dovecot with Roundcube, SFTPGo, and Prometheus telemetry.
  • Full-Stack TypeScript & Verification Discipline: Next.js 16 App Router, React 19 Server Components, Better Auth, zero-downtime Kysely migrations on MariaDB, and strict TDD — verified across over a thousand Vitest unit tests, database integration suites, Playwright E2E and 5-viewport visual-regression checks, axe WCAG 2.2 AA gates, and an 86-check live smoke suite.
  • Local AI, Graphics & Multi-Theme Craft: Streaming SSE RAG pipelines with Ollama, custom Three.js GLSL particle shaders, and fluid token-driven UI calibrated across Obsidian, Blueprint, and Daylight themes from 390 px mobile to 3840 px 4K displays.
  • Release Engineering & Continuity: Atomic on-host release builds with one-command rollback, automated daily backups and weekly scratch-database restore drills across all 9 components, and clear operations documentation.

content:
Use the Open Roundcube Webmail button on this page or go directly to /webmail/. Sign in with your full mailbox address (e.g. username@ytl-nexus.internal) and your mailbox password.

Webmail credentials are separate from your Nexus platform password. If you forgot your mailbox password, an Administrator can reset it in Nexus Control.

title: Configuring your email client
content:
You can connect desktop and mobile mail clients (such as Thunderbird, Apple Mail or Outlook) using standard IMAP and SMTP submission.

  • Incoming (IMAP): port 993, SSL/TLS required.
  • Outgoing (SMTP): port 587, STARTTLS required.
  • Username: your full email address (username@ytl-nexus.internal).
  • Authentication: Normal password.

Nexus uses certificates from the YTL Nexus internal CA. Make sure the CA certificate is installed on your client device.
